study_identification_part.si4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

nm2_1_modeling_method.detail: Age-related normative model of cortical thickness built with local polynomial regression (LOESS); smoothing kernel width chosen by minimizing sum of squared errors via Brent’s method with R optim; model fit on TD males to derive age-specific means/SDs for w-scores.
nm2_1_modeling_method.supporting_text: "We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS)... smoothing kernel of the regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization across 5-100% of the full age range using Brent’s method as implemented in the R optim function"

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Primary normative modelling on cortical thickness averaged within 308 cortical regions; same LOESS-based approach additionally applied to cortical surface area, cortical volume, and gyrification (reported in supplementary analyses).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: "We examined how cortical thickness (CT) in ASD can be parameterized as an individualized metric of atypicality relative to typically-developing (TD) age-related norms"; "All analyses were done on CT averaged within 308 cortical regions"; "To show applicability of this approach we also applied the same method to other measures of neuroanatomy; gyrification, volume and surface area."
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Bethlehem2020.pdf.md: Introduction; Results / Age-related normative modelling; Results / exploratory extensions
